clue.text: They ruminate about ex-PM not reaching a conclusion

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: the surname stops short of its final letter, so the last E is dropped

parts.note: Clement Attlee was a British Prime Minister after the war

explanation.surface: Pundits mull over a former Prime Minister who never quite finished anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not reaching a conclusion' cuts the last letter from ATTLEE, leaving ATTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows chew the cud, so ruminating beasts describes farm herds.

clue.text: Seductress's lacy pants with edging of pearls round

indicators.note: pants as a verb, here read as 'is rubbish', signals the word lacy being jumbled
the edging of a word is its outermost letters, its first and last

parts.note: a round shape resembles the letter O

explanation.surface: A temptress wears lacy underwear trimmed with a ring of pearls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear but is the anagram signal; 'edging of' takes P and S from 'pearls'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Odyssey the nymph of that name detained Odysseus on her island for years, a classic temptress.

clue.text: Son tucked into goose; he sought seconds

indicators.note: the abbreviation for son is placed inside the word for a silly person

parts.note: a goose is a silly person, a twit

explanation.surface: A boy eats his goose dinner, and then wants another helping.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's orphan Oliver famously asked for more gruel, a request for a second helping.

clue.text: The French show attack on Turks

parts.note: le is French for the
a panto, short for pantomime, is a British Christmas stage show

explanation.surface: French forces display an assault on Turkish troops.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto is a British family theatre show staged around Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1571 naval battle of that name saw the Holy League attack and defeat the Ottoman fleet.

clue.text: Bemoan period of doing without cakes before noon

indicators.note: to cake is to coat or encrust, so the season's name wraps around the morning abbreviation

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting and abstinence
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before midday

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a stretch of giving up cakes until lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cakes' looks like the food given up but is a verb meaning 'coats', the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemoan something is to grieve over it, to mourn or wail about it.

clue.text: Patriotic work, extremely American, but not US?

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the opposite side to us is them

explanation.surface: A flag-waving piece is thoroughly American, yet somehow not from the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not US' reads as not the United States but means the pronoun opposite to us.
explanation.definitionFit: A national song sung on patriotic occasions is a piece of music celebrating the country.

clue.text: Strike off priest I meant to reform

parts.note: Eli is the priest of Shiloh in the Book of Samuel

indicators.note: to reform is to make over in a new shape, so the letters of I meant are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman intends to mend his ways and is struck off the register.
explanation.walkthrough: The priest is the Old Testament Eli, a crossword regular; 'to reform' shuffles only the following two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike off a list is to remove or get rid of an item.

clue.text: Fixture to support curtain feature

parts.note: a tie is a scheduled sports match, a fixture
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A fitting is installed to hold up the drapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixture' suggests a fitting, but here it is the sporting sense of a scheduled match.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord or band that holds a drape open at the side is a common window detail.

clue.text: See 14
Magridal Bizet's penned in city by the Tarn

indicators.note: the letters sit enclosed within the run of words Magridal Bizet's

explanation.surface: A musician's piece by Bizet was written in a southern French town.
explanation.definitionFit: This cathedral city in southern France stands on the Tarn river.

clue.text: Longed to receive team's kit with lined motif

indicators.note: the word for longed takes in the kit word, holding it inside

parts.note: to pine is to long, so longed is pined
a team's strip is its matching kit of shirts and shorts

explanation.surface: A fan yearned to get the club's shirts, which have a striped pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: A strip is British usage for a sports team's uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric patterned with very thin parallel lines, as in a banker's suit, has this description.

clue.text: Exactly what the bare-bosomed have rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: the topless have no tops on

explanation.surface: A question about what topless sunbathers have turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns NO TOPS around.
explanation.definitionFit: Something precisely right is accurate to the dot, quite correct.

clue.text: Perish, then arise miraculously in this hymn?

parts.note: to perish is to die

indicators.note: a miracle transforms things, so the letters of arise are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hymn about dying and then rising again by a miracle, as in resurrection.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the surface story of death and resurrection fits the hymn's subject, Judgement Day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin 'day of wrath' sequence is a medieval hymn sung in the Requiem Mass.

clue.text: Head of municipality to pull in favours for thriving areas

indicators.note: the leading letter and the pulling word go inside the word for favours

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to tow is to pull along

explanation.surface: A mayor uses grants to drag in investment for prosperous districts.
explanation.definitionFit: Places enjoying a sudden economic surge are prosperous, fast-growing settlements.

clue.text: Fuss over Madonna, due back on a stage to be choreographed

indicators.note: choreography arranges dancers' moves, so all these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: The pop star Madonna is set to return to the stage with a routine planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be choreographed' rearranges all twenty-two letters of MADONNA DUE BACK ON A STAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make an unnecessary commotion over something, to fuss.

clue.text: See 16
It's easy to rouse Irish port, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: to rouse someone is to wake them
Cork is a port city in southern Ireland

explanation.surface: A boast that waking up a whole Irish port city would be no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of WAKE CORK gives CAKE WORK, which in British speech sounds like CAKE WALK, as 'cork' and 'walk' rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Something effortless is a cinch, a very simple task or victory.

clue.text: Composer's moving tear, captivated by French horn

indicators.note: being captivated means held captive, so the French horn holds the jumbled letters inside it

parts.note: cor is the French word for horn

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters of tear being shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: A composer sheds an emotional tear, entranced by the sound of a French horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges TEAR into REAT; 'French horn' is not the instrument but COR, French for horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer is one who makes or originates something, a maker.

clue.text: Bacterium gets bought, we're told, or gametes

parts.note: a bacterium is a germ

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard rather than read, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a product that gets bought sells

explanation.surface: A microbe is sold to customers, or perhaps reproductive cells are.
explanation.definitionFit: Sperm and egg cells, the reproductive cells that fuse at fertilisation, are the gametes.

clue.text: Speechless about group's bagpipe

indicators.note: the word for speechless goes around the group word

parts.note: someone speechless is mute
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Someone left speechless by a band's bagpipe playing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small French bellows-blown bagpipe, popular at the court of Louis XIV.

clue.text: What may soothe infant with head dropping

definitions.text: What may soothe infant with head dropping

parts.note: to lull is to soothe

indicators.note: the head of the word for an infant drops away, losing its first letter

parts.note: an infant is a baby

explanation.surface: A gentle song soothes a baby until its head nods off to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a baby whose head drops is falling asleep to the song.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft song sung to send a baby off to sleep is the soothing item described.

clue.text: Hum and turn round — that is rhythmic music

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell, and BO stands for body odour

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word for turn is reversed

parts.note: a go is a turn
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Instructions to hum a tune and spin around, as for dance music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hum' looks musical but is the British slang for a stink, giving BO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fast blues-based piano style also called boogie-woogie, a dance rhythm.

clue.text: Sacrifice no time in playing Bach motet

indicators.note: playing a piece of music performs it in a new way, so the remaining letters are rearranged
no means without, so one letter for time is removed

explanation.surface: Sacrificing time to perform a choral work by Bach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no time' takes one T from BACH MOTET, and 'playing' rearranges what remains into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a great public sacrifice, originally of a hundred oxen, bore this name.

clue.text: Symbol of peasant's morbid and empty life

parts.note: morbid humour is sick

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving just its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A peasant's existence is described as grim and hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved harvesting blade, paired with the hammer, emblemised Soviet farm workers.

clue.text: Motor lubricant but not one for a girl

parts.note: a motor is a car

indicators.note: but not means the numeral for one is removed from the lubricant

parts.note: oil is a lubricant
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: Car oil, but not a single can of it, for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common female first name, here standing for any girl.

clue.text: Tenor disheartened in melody fit to be forte

indicators.note: the outer letters of tenor go inside the word for melody

parts.note: a song is a melody

indicators.note: disheartened removes the heart of the word, keeping only its outer letters

parts.note: to suit is to fit

explanation.surface: A dispirited tenor is in a tune that suits him, sung loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves TR from Tenor, which goes into SONG; 'forte' looks musical (loud) but means one's speciality.
explanation.definitionFit: One's speciality or area of real skill is the thing one does best.

clue.text: Stern king with sensitivity for music

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
having an ear for music means being sensitive to it

explanation.surface: A severe monarch who is also musically gifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like an adjective meaning severe, but it is the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern of a vessel is its back end, its hind part.

clue.text: They collect scraps of some early jazz pieces

parts.note: ragtime is an early jazz style, and a rag is a piece of it
men are pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: Collectors gathering fragments of old jazz recordings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scraps' looks like the jazz fragments; it means waste cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealers who gather old cloth and rubbish to sell on are rag-and-bone collectors.

clue.text: Tinker half-heartedly with perfumery's ultimate potpourri

indicators.note: the word's heart is a double letter, and only half of that pair is kept

parts.note: to tinker with something is to meddle

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its last

explanation.surface: Fiddling lazily with a scent shop's final fragrant mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two central Ds of MEDDLE, leaving MEDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixture of assorted items is a jumble or miscellany, much like a dried-petal blend.
